candidate.rationale:
Diagnosis: the registered source's fmt() emitted bare tokens ("walk shed location1 bob") while the interface mandates a parenthesized string per action. That mismatch explains both historical observations (error_kind=operator_syntax, failed_at index 0, executed_actions 0 — rejected before any action was simulated, with no unsatisfied goals/preconditions reported because parsing never succeeded). The registered whitespace-normalization probe explicitly forbids adding parentheses, so it could not have repaired this; verdict would be unknown rather than supported.

Single intended edit: fmt() now returns "(walk l1 l2 m)", "(pickup_spanner l s m)", "(tighten_nut l s m n)" — argument order unchanged from the domain schemas. Secondary hardening: per-type object tables are sorted before use so grounding and successor ordering do not depend on set iteration order (the task text warns against relying on it); tighten_nut's precondition guard order was reorganized but the atom set is identical.

Uncertainty: the fix is inferred from the required output format plus the operator_syntax signal; I have not observed a passing replay. VAL may additionally require a specific spacing convention or reject plans that carry extra/nested text, and it is possible the host's syntax check needs no parentheses at all in some other convention. If VAL applies a nullary-effect/typing nuance that my effects omit, replay could still fail. These are development expectations only; no claim is made about held-out instances or about sufficiency of parentheses for any other error class.

auxiliary.edit: fmt() wraps each action in parentheses; deterministic sorted grounding
auxiliary.registered_probe_conclusion: The registered whitespace-only normalization cannot apply: fmt() emits no parentheses, and the probe contract forbids adding them. Its verdict for this failure mode would be unknown, not supported.
residual_risks: VAL spacing/syntax convention may differ from single-space-inside-parens
effects modeled as add-wins; could differ if a precondition atom reappears
BFS may exceed node cap on larger hidden instances
